trust_decision.summary: No trust boundary is enforced at the HTML directory-listing sink: generate_directory_html splices filesystem/embedded entry names and the raw request URI path into markup with format!, and its only consumer (Html(String) -> Html<T>) does not escape either, so every untrusted value reaches the browser verbatim; the published fix moves the decision into the renderer by routing all values through IntoHtml::escape_and_write (html! macros) and building row hrefs via Uri::path_mut().push_segment.

landing_point.why: The report names unescaped file names and URI path in the ServeDir HTML directory listing; an engineer lands directly on generate_directory_html and the format! row template at :758-770 that splices entry.name into both the link text and the href attribute.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Only interpolated values may be escaped: escaping the finished page (or escaping again at Html(payload)) double-escapes the static <tr>/<table> template and destroys the listing, and over-encoding breaks working links - `&` and `'` must stay literal in the href (percent-encoded set is only URI-unsafe bytes) and then be attribute-escaped exactly once, so `a&b.txt` yields href="/a&b.txt" and display text "a&b.txt". Additionally rama-http must keep building with its default (empty) feature set: pub mod html is gated at rama-http/src/lib.rs:34-36, so an unconditional use of crate::html in open_file.rs breaks `cargo build -p rama-http`.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An HTML 404 / fallback body that echoes the requested URI path instead of the bare not_found() status.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: future.rs already owns response building for OpenFileOutput and the fallback branch holds the original Request, so a maintainer adding a branded 404 page would splice req.uri().path() into markup exactly the way the listing did.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second HTML renderer that builds its page as a String and hands it to Html<T> (e.g. a listing/status page next to the file listing).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Html<T> accepts any T: Into<Body> and performs no escaping at that layer, so any new String-building renderer silently inherits the flaw; a maintainer writing 'one more small HTML page' beside the listing is the natural mistake.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An HTML error page for rejected/not-found paths that echoes the requested (possibly percent-decoded) path back to the client.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the invalid-path branch where the raw request URI is still in hand and the user-visible message 'you asked for <path>' is exactly what a maintainer would render.

O9_family: improper output encoding / escaping (CWE-116) leading to stored and reflected cross-site scripting (CWE-79)
